title: Pell Confesses
warm:
Pell confesses partially meant [player_name] stood in hangar cold while Marcus Pell spent traveling into half-truths that still refused to settle Vivienne. Early thirties, she/her, across-the-hall neighbor—Nolan Greer bruised lightly from the breach, Detective Imani Brooks's homicide interest rising without a body. Four fates open: willing leave, paid vanish, dead, staging. Partial confession did not force any of them.

"I managed exits," Pell said, NDA language cracking. "Not a corpse. Not a sole fate. Soft alibi still fits if you want it to." Nolan's cufflinks clicked once—tell alive—then stilled. Wind sheer was memory. Elevator chime was Crownspire. Unused perfume still haunted [player_name]'s coat. Rhea Quinn's slate had never owned this hangar, but Brooks would invent a path from slate to fuel if asked.

[player_name] did not invent death from Pell's half-mouth. She did not invent Milan. Partial confession only proved silence had been purchased—and that Vivienne's cadence could still be method or coincidence depending on which fear she fed. Soft meant pliable evidence with attorney aftertaste.

Black car. Wine rings memory. Hope and dread shared the hangar.

"Hospital or lobby dawn with Nolan," she heard herself cataloguing, "or mercy-rewrite what you'll swear from what Pell half-gave. Neither settles Vivienne. Both spend the partial."

She catalogued Pell's confession the way Brooks would: half-truth, no forced fate, soft still claimed. [player_name] felt traveling language dying in her ears, and understood that partial truth had already changed which soft she could still swear.
